evidence: Written and verified in the authoring session, not recalled: tools/nvidia/nim.py (all ~260 lines, authored 2026-07-29) mirrors tools/openrouter/client.py, which was read via its own prior-art record's per-line citations rather than in full this session; tools/lib/quota.py was read in full (121 lines) and tools/lib/envload.py in full (196 lines) before reuse. The endpoint behavior is measured, not quoted from docs: `python tools/nvidia/nim.py selftest --live` fetched the real catalogue and returned a real 200 completion (9/9 checks) under the operator's key on 2026-07-29. The claim that NVIDIA publishes no numeric per-day free ceiling is from memory and is NOT verified against current terms; the 100/day ceiling is therefore recorded as local policy in the module docstring. Alternatives below were assessed from prior sessions' fetched records (LiteLLM budgets-need-Postgres is quoted by the tools-openrouter record from a 2026-07-29 fetch) and from training knowledge where marked; none was installed or run this session.
recheck: 1) Is the channel still live and free: `python tools/nvidia/nim.py selftest --live` must return 9/9 with a 200 completion and `python tools/lib/quota.py nvidia 100` must show the ledger counting. 2) Does the OpenAI-SDK alternative now cover the retained property: search its release notes for client-side daily-budget/ledger support; if it ships one, the transport half of nim.py is dead code and the verdict flips to adopt-plus-keep-ledger. 3) Re-read NVIDIA's rate-limit page and replace the local-policy ceiling with the vendor number if one now exists.
why: nim.py is ~250 lines and deliberately duplicates the SHAPE of tools/openrouter/client.py (same _http, same catalogue-cache-pick, same quota reuse) rather than abstracting the two into a shared base, because the openrouter prior-art record already established that the bespoke half of that file is the quota ledger and exit-code contracts, both of which live in tools/lib and ARE reused here. The only new code is NVIDIA-specific: the integrate.api.nvidia.com endpoint, a preference order for NIM slugs, and a --logprobs passthrough. The reason a second client exists at all is refuter diversity: a second vendor's free pool with a separate quota bucket and separate failure domain, serving weight families OpenRouter's free tier rotates out. The operator's original framing was 'access to model weights and looking inside models'; that is recorded here as explicitly NOT what this component provides. NIM preview endpoints are hosted inference; token logprobs are the only interior signal, and only where an endpoint exposes them. Weights come from Hugging Face downloads, a different task not owned by this component.

alternatives.name: OpenAI Python SDK pointed at integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1
alternatives.covers: the transport completely; NVIDIA documents OpenAI-compatibility for its chat completions surface, so base_url plus api_key gives typed responses, retries, and streaming.
alternatives.gap: no local daily ceiling or pacing before dispatch, no append-only usage ledger, no 'a 429 does not count' accounting, which is the property this repo's quota.py exists for. Pulls httpx/pydantic into a stdlib-only repo to replace ~25 lines of urllib.
alternatives.maturity: first-party, maintained; not installed or version-checked this session.

alternatives.name: LiteLLM SDK (docs.litellm.ai), which lists nvidia_nim as a supported provider
alternatives.covers: the call surface across both this client and tools/openrouter in one dependency, with client-side fallbacks.
alternatives.gap: same finding as the tools-openrouter record: budgets and rate limits are Proxy-only and its own docs require a Postgres database for them, which is a server plus a database to replace the JSONL ledger for a single-maintainer offline repo.
alternatives.cost: large pip dependency; Proxy adoption is a running server plus Postgres.
alternatives.maturity: current and widely covered; not installed this session.

alternatives.name: tools/openrouter itself (already in this repo)
alternatives.covers: the second-opinion job as such; some NIM-hosted families also appear on OpenRouter free.
alternatives.gap: one vendor's free tier is one rate-limit bucket and one catalogue policy; when it 429s or rotates a family out, the refutation channel goes dark. A second pool is the point, not a duplicate.
alternatives.cost: zero; the gap is structural, not effort.

alternatives.name: Hugging Face weight downloads (huggingface_hub) for the 'inside the model' half
alternatives.covers: the operator's stated interest in weights and interpretability: actual safetensors, activations via local forward passes, hooks into layers.
alternatives.gap: a different project entirely: tens to hundreds of GB per model, local GPU or CPU-offload constraints, and nothing about it is an API client. Deliberately not started; if interpretability work becomes real it should be its own proposal with disk and hardware math attached.
alternatives.maturity: huggingface_hub is mature; the constraint is local hardware, unverified on this machine.
